newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's 1997 privatisation funds to equal 1996.
newsitem.headline: France's 1997 privatisation funds to equal 1996.

text.p: Budget Minister Alain Lamassoure said on Saturday that France would take in 27 billion francs ($5.3 billion) from next year's privatisation sales and said all of the funds would be put into the hard-pressed public sector.

"The difficult situation in which the public-sector businesses find themselves justifies giving them all of the proceeds expected from privatisations during 1997 -- on the order of 27 billion francs," Lamassoure told parliament during debate on next year's state budget.

He said beneficiaries would include coal mining interests, arms maker GIAT, Credit Lyonnais and a new state-owned holding company being set up to assume some of the railwyy system's debt and to take over ownership of France's rail infrastructure.
The government had previously announced that this year's take from privatisations would be about 27 billion francs.
Lamassoure's Saturday announcement was the first indication that the state planned to make the same amount of money next year as well.
